ut_cove_the.blurb: The Cove is a modest sport crag tucked into the trees on the north side of the Right Fork of Maple Canyon, up the hillside from the main trail. It holds ten bolted routes on conglomerate, from a single 5.5 and a few 5.7s through 5.8 and 5.9 to about four lines in the 5.10 range, so it suits newer leaders and intermediate climbers alike. Bolts and anchors are sturdy stainless. The wall faces southeast and catches sun through the middle of the day, which makes spring and fall the comfortable seasons. It feels like a quiet step away from the busier walls nearby, and the walk up from the road is short.

ut_crack_boulder.blurb: Crack Boulder is a roadside sandstone block in the Left Fork of Joe's Valley, close to a campground and easy to spot from the road. A crack runs right through it, splitting the rock into two distinct faces. About ten problems are on offer, mostly easy to moderate: one or two near V0, several at V2 and V3, plus a couple of harder tests for stronger climbers. That makes it a handy spot for warming up before heading to bigger boulders. The cracks themselves are some of the best-liked lines here, and the block sees little traffic.

ut_eco_terrorist_wall.blurb: Eco-Terrorist Wall is a compact sport crag in the lower part of Maple Canyon, perched a couple of hundred feet above the canyon floor on the buttress and gully beside Anti-Gravity Rock. Its ten routes are bolted conglomerate lines spanning roughly 5.7 to 5.11, with most falling between 5.8 and 5.10 and two lines at the 5.11 level. A few of the lines stand out as favourites while the rest are gentler, so it works for a relaxed day with a mixed group. Routes begin in a gully and wrap around the buttress.

ut_getaway_wall_the.blurb: The Getaway Wall sits beside Notch Lake high in the Uinta Mountains, around 10,000 feet, on the southwest side of the water. You reach it by following the south shore until the cliff rises in front of you. Ten routes mix sport and trad, with seven bolted lines and three on gear. Grades run from an easy 5.6 through 5.9 and 5.10 to a handful of 5.11s, and the sport lines are mostly in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. The alpine lake setting is the main draw, making it a pleasant escape from lower, hotter crags.
